data.name: Makhtoom
data.gender_notes: Makhtoom is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is concealed or hidden from others. The name Makhtoom carries the meaning “The Veiled One” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Makhtoom usually hope their child will grow to embody the veiled one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Makhtoom total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: مختوم
in_arabic.meaning: مختوم تعني المختتم والمؤتمن على شيء ما
in_arabic.long_meaning: مختوم هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و يعني المختتم والمؤتمن على شيء ما، وهو من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني الاختتام والاكتمال. وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم ذكر الاختتام والختام في عدة مواضع، مما يعطي هذا الاسم قيمة روحية ودينية كبيرة.

in_urdu.name: مختوم
in_urdu.meaning: مختوم کا مطلب ہے مہتمن اور محافظ
in_urdu.long_meaning: مختوم ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے مہتمن اور محافظ۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقالید میں بہت اہمیت رکھتا ہے کیونکہ یہ احتیاط اور امانت کی علامت ہے۔ اس کا ذکر جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی معاشرے میں بھی کیا جاتا ہے جہاں یہ نام احترام اور ذمہ داری کے ساتھ منسلک ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मख्तूम
in_hindi.meaning: मख्तूम का अर्थ है संरक्षक और रक्षक
in_hindi.long_meaning: मख्तूम एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है संरक्षक और रक्षक। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत महत्व रखता है क्योंकि यह सुरक्षा और विश्वास की भावना को दर्शाता है। इस नाम का उपयोग पारंपरिक और आधुनिक दोनों संदर्भों में किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: مختوم
in_pashto.meaning: مختوم د محافظ او امین معنی دی
in_pashto.long_meaning: مختوم د عربي اصل څخه يو نوم دی چې د محافظ او امین معنی دی. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون قومونو په دودو او رسموں کې ډیر اهمیت لري ځکه چې دا د امانت او پاملرنې نښه ده.

in_english.name: Makhtoom
in_english.meaning: Makhtoom means sealed, stamped, or a trustworthy guardian
in_english.long_meaning: The name Makhtoom is derived from the Arabic root 'kha-ta-ma,' which means to seal or to stamp. In Islamic tradition, it signifies a trustworthy guardian or someone who is sealed or stamped with approval. The name holds spiritual significance as it relates to concepts of trust, responsibility, and divine approval.

data.cultural_impact: The name Makhtoom, though less commonly used, holds significant cultural importance in Islamic society. Historically, it is believed to have been the name of a famous Sufi saint named Shah Abdul Qadir Jilani. He was a prominent scholar, mystic, and founder of the Qadriya Sufi order. The term Makhtoom was used to describe his transcendental state where he was physically present but spiritually detached, enshrouded in deep mystical contemplation.
data.spiritual_significance: Makhtoom, as a spiritual designation, denotes a state of complete surrender and submission to the divine will, a stage where the individual is devoid of any self-centeredness or ego. The person, in such a state, is completely hidden from the material sight of the world, immersed in a realm of solitude and communion with the divine.
